current_answer: Jev is TypeSafe AI's hosted model for bounded Choice, Score and Noul judgments; your code must check each answer and own the action, review and fallback. As of 11 October 2026, 05:17 UTC, Jev is available to new users: signups have been open since 27 September (TypeSafe CEO's post), new accounts get no free credit, and the API is operational (status page); the pool did not observe signup itself because the console returns HTTP 403. TypeSafe lists jev-1.13.0 at $0.042 per million input tokens with free output; its published rate limits are now 100K tokens per second and 80 requests per second (the request limit was 40 per second from 30 September until at least 2 October 05:14 UTC; the exact time of the change is unknown). OpenRouter, Cloudflare, Vercel, Netlify and Opper serve it at the same or rounded list price, while lookalike reseller storefronts charged 3–16× that price. On the six routes whose data terms were read, no primary text allows training on your prompts without consent; TypeSafe's MCA grants it a licence in perpetuity to use Customer Data to derive telemetry and to monitor for fraud and abuse, states no retention period and offers zero data retention to enterprise customers; its trust center lists 6 subprocessors (Nebius and CoreWeave added 2 October, where prompts are "processed, but not stored" in TypeSafe's wording), while OpenRouter, Cloudflare and Vercel label the TypeSafe provider zero-retention; Vercel lists two providers for Jev (checked 10 Oct 2026, 05:12 UTC; unchanged since 6 Oct), TypeSafe AI (zero data retention) and DigitalOcean (no zero data retention), and picks between them by uptime and latency unless you set the provider order (a reading of the text, not legal advice). On 4 of 6 routes read on 6 Oct 2026 you can write a versioned Jev ID; Vercel and Cloudflare take only an unversioned one, and jev-latest points to jev-1.13.0 on TypeSafe's models page. Published benchmarks, all Reported and graded A–D, disagree because they test different tasks: Jev is usually ahead of cheap LLM setups that generate their answer as text (one grade-B study found open-weight models scored through their token probabilities about level with it overall), close to frontier LLM judges on verdicts that can be read off the text once a threshold is tuned, and behind the best LLMs on derived judgments; TypeSafe's published 67.8% is agreement with LLM reference answers, not accuracy against human labels. No published moderation accuracy for Jev was found. Jev weights or a local Jev runtime published by TypeSafe were not found on TypeSafe's site, docs, GitHub organisation or a Hugging Face author search (10 Oct 2026, 05:11–05:20 UTC); TypeSafe's docs say "the same weights serve every account", and Jev-named models on Hugging Face come from other accounts. The alternatives page lists 31 substitutes by the layer they replace (12 model weights, 11 local runtimes, 4 request adapters, 2 classifier or LLM approaches, and 2 hosted APIs from other providers: OpenAI's Decisions API in public beta and Microsoft-Decision-1). Two independent grade-A comparisons of Jev with OpenAI's Decisions API differ by task: the Decisions API is ahead on RPG move choices (B38); Jev is ahead on exact judge score in Portuguese and level on routing and injection (B39); the pool states no overall parity. Among open alternatives, only Opper's 362-item test puts one open model, Kev-4B, within noise of Jev (Opper hosts Kev); JevBench scores Laya and earlier Kev previews well below Jev. Code read at pinned commits shows how projects handle Jev failures: of five support-ticket triage projects, four send unsure tickets to a person and one files tickets in its archive lane on any Jev API error; of six self-hosted Jev model routers, one sends every Jev failure to its frontier model and five keep the current model, pick locally or choose no model, while OpenRouter does not document what its Jev Router does when Jev fails; of six moderation projects, four leave the post up or let it through when the Jev call fails, one holds it for a person and one returns no decision; of five email and lead sorters, none changes the mailbox when Jev errors, and of the 3 that can write to Gmail or IMAP only 1 routes unsure mail to a Review label; of 4 Jev trading bots, 2 can still place a new order when Jev errors and all 4 can trade without Jev, while none of 3 fraud or payment gates moves money; of 4 Jev judge tools, DeepEval stops the run on a Jev error and the other 3 drop the item from the score, with openlayer jevals still reporting it as passed. Of 7 Jev browser and computer-use agents read in source, none clicks or types when Jev errors, but 5 act on low-confidence answers and only 1 asks a person before send, buy or delete; of 6 Jev framework packages, 4 are pre-1.0 and none comes from TypeSafe, 4 raise Jev errors to the caller, while the community Spring AI filter and the LlamaIndex reranker fail open. Of 24 Jev coding-agent integrations (Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Claude Code) read in source, 1 is vendor-published (OpenClaw) and none comes from TypeSafe; 13 act on Jev's answer, 10 do not and 1 is unsettled; on a Jev error the 13: 5 let the call run, 3 hold the call and 5 fall back to another model or the host's original path (one of them, jev-approvals, may ask the main agent model, which can approve). Across 74 implementations in 11 use cases (eval judges counted from 7 October, rerankers and document pipelines from 8 October, coding-agent rows added on 10 and 11 October), on a Jev error 38 stop or hold the action, 20 fall back, 8 let it through unchecked (4 moderation bots, 2 agent hooks, a passage filter and the openlayer jevals eval tool, whose report counts an errored eval as passed), 5 return no decision and 3 are advisory; the action goes ahead in 15 of 74. For reranking, the grade-A relevance-judgment study (iwhalen) measures relevance judgments, not reranking; of 4 rerunnable graded reranking-pipeline studies, 2 come from parties with a stake and 2 state none (jev-pulse: 40 queries, BM25-only baseline; jev-rerank-bench: Jev level with Cohere Rerank 4 Pro within noise, graded A on 11 October); of 5 reranking and passage-filter implementations, on a Jev error 2 stop, 2 fall back and 1 passes unscreened passages. Of 5 SQL and document-pipeline projects, all 5 stop the query or request on a Jev error, pg-redact also stores text unredacted when a span's answer is missing or below 0.5, and all 5 send row or document text out. Jev is not listed in the Amazon Bedrock model catalog or the Azure AI Foundry model catalog (checked 5 Oct 2026, 05:18–05:19 UTC), and TypeSafe's docs mention neither; teams on AWS or Azure call TypeSafe's API or a gateway. Python and TypeScript have official SDKs (typesafe-sdk 0.7.2 as audited, 0.7.4 published 9 October, both defaulting to 10 s per HTTP operation and 2 retries; @typesafe-ai/sdk 0.6.0, 10,000 ms per attempt and 2 retries); of five Claude Code and MCP guardrails first read in source, only LangChain's AutoModeMiddleware fails closed (two more read later: jev-permission-gate falls back to Claude Code's built-in classifier, and jev-llm-guard only returns a verdict), @jkudish/jev-mcp keeps its audited advisory failure path (checked at 0.14.1), and oh-my-claudecode is advisory at default settings, with its failure path checked at v5.6.2 and a 2,000 ms default timeout (250 ms up to v5.5.0). TypeSafe's own n8n node is the scoped @typesafe-ai/n8n-nodes-typesafe-ai (npm provenance, n8n-verified); the unscoped n8n-nodes-typesafe-ai is a third party's, and all 5 n8n nodes read stop the workflow on a Jev error by default. Of 99 Products ledger rows (11 October), the pool read the Jev call in source for 86; none of the 99, nor 7 published claims, is independently verified as running in production.

catalogue_card.question: What can I build with Jev, what alternatives exist, and where can I use it at what cost?
catalogue_card.text: Question-ordered pages on Jev (TypeSafe AI): current access status and notices, use cases including support-ticket triage, model routing, content moderation, email and lead sorting, trading and fraud gates, Jev as an eval judge and browser and computer-use agents, what implementations do when Jev fails, demo videos, graded benchmarks, Jev vs Laya vs Kev, Jev vs LLM vs classifier, data retention and training by route, limits, build guides including the n8n node, framework and coding-agent integrations, errors, confidence thresholds, reseller checks, model IDs and aliases by route, cost per decision, routes including whether Jev is on Amazon Bedrock or Azure AI Foundry, projects and open alternatives, each with evidence labels and check dates.

summary: Access (checked 11 Oct 2026, 05:17 UTC): signups open since 27 Sep 2026, 22:33 UTC (CEO post); no free credit for new users; API operational since 29 Sep, 22:05 UTC (status page; 90-day API uptime 99.838%). The pool did not observe signup: the console returned HTTP 403.
Jev answers from a fixed answer set: Choice (up to 255 options), Score (up to 10 levels), Noul (probability of yes). It does not generate text and accepts text input only.

List price $0.042/M input, output free on TypeSafe, OpenRouter, Cloudflare and (in its models API) Vercel; Opper and Vercel's web page round to $0.04; Netlify bills credits. Lookalike resellers displayed 3–16× the list price.

TypeSafe's published rate limits are 100K tokens per second and 80 requests per second (checked 11 Oct, 05:17 UTC; unchanged since 3 Oct). The request limit was 40 per second from 30 Sep until at least 2 Oct, 05:14 UTC; before 30 Sep the page listed 250,000 tokens/s and 1,200 requests/min. Neither change has an exact time.

Data handling (quoted 1 Oct, not legal advice): no route's text allows training on prompts without consent; TypeSafe's MCA grants a licence in perpetuity to use Customer Data to derive telemetry and to monitor for fraud and abuse; no TypeSafe retention period is stated; ZDR is offered directly to enterprise customers.

Subprocessors (read 4 Oct, unchanged 11 Oct): TypeSafe's trust center lists 6 (Amazon Web Services, Modal, Slack, Google Workspace, Nebius, CoreWeave); Nebius and CoreWeave were added on 2 Oct; prompts are "processed, but not stored" on Modal, Nebius and CoreWeave compute nodes (TypeSafe's wording). A SOC 2 Type II resource is listed behind "Request access"; the report was not seen.

Zero data retention by layer: OpenRouter's gateway is ZDR by default and lists the TypeSafe endpoint as ZDR; Cloudflare lists ZDR 'Yes' but AI Gateway logs are on by default; Vercel marks TypeSafe AI ZDR but also routes Jev through DigitalOcean, marked not ZDR; Opper says ZDR is not established for its TypeSafe route.

Jev vs Laya vs Kev: only Opper's 362-item test (B11) puts an open model, Kev-4B, within noise of Jev, and Opper hosts Kev; JevBench (B07) scores Laya 23.0–41.7 and earlier Kev previews 53.8–59.7 against Jev's 80.0. All Reported.

Laya and Kev weights are Apache-2.0; Kev's Qwen bases are Apache-2.0; Laya's card metadata names no base. Laya's English checkpoint reads 512 tokens and its multilingual checkpoint ships uncalibrated; Kev is English-only.

Support-ticket triage, five projects read at pinned commits: four gate on confidence (0.5–0.9) and send unsure tickets to a person; one ignores queue confidence and archives tickets on API errors; only one validates answers; two set no timeout.

Model routing (2 Oct): OpenRouter documents how its Jev Router narrows candidates, but not what it does when Jev fails, is unsure or gets a long conversation, nor how the routed model is billed. Of six self-hosted Jev routers read at pinned commits (chosen by GitHub stars), one sends every Jev failure to its frontier model; one keeps the current model; two pick locally; two choose no model.

Content moderation (2 Oct): of six projects read at pinned commits (five code-backed integrations, one runnable demo), four leave the post up or let it through when the Jev call fails, one holds it for a person (WordPress) and one returns no decision. Two have a pardon that lifts the punishment but does not restore the message; four send author data beyond the text by default. No published moderation accuracy was found.

Email and lead sorting (3 Oct): of 5 sorters read at pinned commits (chosen by GitHub stars plus one lead project), none changes the mailbox when Jev errors; 3 can write to the mailbox and only 1 of those sends unsure mail to a Review label; none has delete or trash code. Cost per 1,000 emails by pool arithmetic: about $0.025 for very short emails and $0.04–$0.15 at the projects' body cuts; a Reported demo works out to $0.106.

Trading and fraud gates (4 Oct): of 4 Jev trading bots read at pinned commits, 2 can still place a new order when Jev errors (QuantDinger after an LLM fallback; btc-hft-jev through a rules-only path) and all 4 can trade without Jev; all 4 default to mock, paper, testnet or a virtual account, and in two bots "mock" means no Jev, not no trading. None of 3 fraud or payment gates has a payment call site. No trade, payment or performance figure was checked.

When Jev fails (11 Oct): across 74 implementations in 11 use cases (the 10 Oct table plus jev-triage, the jev-for-all launcher and hermes-jev-mana under Coding agents, all routing fallbacks; the three SQL extensions listed but not counted), on a Jev error 38 stop or hold the action, 20 fall back, 8 let it through, 5 return no decision and 3 are advisory; the 8 that let it through are 4 content-moderation bots, 2 agent hooks, one Spring AI passage filter and openlayer jevals; the action goes ahead in 15 of 74 (8 fail-open plus 7 fallbacks). No-key behaviour is not recorded for 18 (LanceDB's no-key cell was read on 11 Oct: fail-closed) and bypass for 33. A copyable checklist repeats the eight questions and counts.

Jev as a judge (4 Oct): of 4 judge tools read at pinned commits, DeepEval stops the run on a Jev error by default; the other 3 drop the item from the score and openlayer jevals still reports it as passed; 1 of 4 codes an escalation for unsure verdicts (opt-in). Judge studies B02, B06 and B08 are Reported; the pool ran no eval.

Browser and computer use (5 Oct): of 7 Jev agents that click, type or tap, read at pinned commits, none acts when Jev errors; 5 act on low-confidence answers (no threshold), 2 block below 0.65 or 0.5; only 1 (Ulka) asks a person before send, buy or delete; 5 of 7 run in the user's own browser, phone or desktop session by default; ironbee-express replays a cached recording unjudged with no key. second-look recommends only and is counted on the checklist; trycua/cua is listed, not counted.

Framework integrations (5 Oct): of 6 packages read at pinned tags (langchain-typesafe 0.0.1a3, @langchain/typesafe 0.0.2, Pydantic AI TypeSafeModel in v2.54.0, @effect/ai-typesafe 4.0.1, community typesafe-spring-ai 0.4.0, community llama-index-postprocessor-jev 0.1.1), 4 are pre-1.0 and none comes from TypeSafe; 4 raise Jev errors to the caller; the Spring AI passage filter and the LlamaIndex reranker fail open; the LangChain middlewares fail closed. pydantic-ai-slim checked at 2.55.0 (11 Oct): failure path unchanged; image input now raises UserError before the request.

Amazon Bedrock and Azure AI Foundry (5 Oct): Jev is not listed in the Bedrock model cards (19 providers, 05:18 UTC) or the Azure AI Foundry catalog (0 models for "typesafe" and "jev", 05:19 UTC); TypeSafe's llms-full.txt mentions neither. Teams call TypeSafe's API or a gateway, so data leaves the cloud's model boundary. A lookalike reseller's "Jev on AWS Bedrock" page is not a source.

Coding agents (11 Oct): Of 24 integrations read in source, 13 act on Jev's answer, 10 do not, 1 is unsettled. On a Jev error the 13: 5 let the call run, 3 hold, 5 fall back. The three newly counted rows: jev-triage (OpenClaw, 6360e21; host code read at aa6008a) sends the message to the main model on every failure; the jev-for-all launcher (npm 0.7.1) uses its default tier on every failure, while its OpenCode plugin part is not settled; hermes-jev-mana (Hermes, 3daf639) runs the original Hermes branch on a Jev failure and is inert after the documented install (every Jev call is refused because admit_unlabeled defaults to false). Hoppin-Sorter/jev-router is not settled (the Claude Code engine's handling of its model rewrite is not public source). 3 of the 13 counted rows do nothing until switched on. 1 of 24 is vendor-published (OpenClaw) and none comes from TypeSafe.

Model IDs and aliases (6 Oct; rechecked unchanged 11 Oct): TypeSafe, Netlify and Opper accept jev-1.13.0 and OpenRouter typesafe/jev-1.13 (minor version only); Vercel (typesafe-ai/jev) and Cloudflare (typesafe/jev) accept only an unversioned ID. jev-latest and jev-preview both point to jev-1.13.0 on TypeSafe's undated models page ("There is no preview build available right now"); TypeSafe advises pinning the version ID instead of an alias. On 10 Oct OpenRouter's typesafe/jev-1.13 endpoint stated a 64,000-token context with a 32,000-token prompt limit (32,000 on 8 Oct).

Drift (11 Oct): pydantic-ai-slim checked at 2.55.0 (failure path unchanged); patch releases @effect/ai-typesafe 4.0.3 (audited 4.0.1), @openclaw/typesafe 2026.10.1 (the jev-triage host branch has the same effect up to the line read), LiteLLM 1.104.2 (read at 1.104.0), typesafe-sdk 0.7.4, ai 7.0.137 and @ai-sdk/typesafe-ai 3.0.17, not re-audited. oh-my-claudecode v5.6.2, @jkudish/jev-mcp 0.14.1, deepeval 4.2.8, jevals 0.1.4, jev-reranker 0.1.2 and lancedb 0.40.0 are still current.

Benchmarks (7 Oct; updated 8, 10 and 11 Oct): 37 rows graded A–D with flags (A 10, B 12, C 8, D 7). Two independent grade-A comparisons of Jev with OpenAI's Decisions API differ by task: Decisions API ahead on RPG move choices (B38); Jev ahead on exact judge score in Portuguese, level on routing and injection (B39). In B39 the Decisions API is ahead within ±1 point (100.0% vs 98.7%) and on injection precision, and the operator calls the routing and injection differences not significant. B40 (jev-rerank-bench) is a reranking-pipeline study in which Jev and Cohere Rerank 4 Pro are within noise. B38–B40 were graded from metric and results files opened at pinned commits on 11 Oct; classifier-bakeoff is a lead, not graded (metric code not opened); a TypeSafe customer case study is a vendor lead; all results Reported; the pool ran none. Against trained classifiers on fixed label sets the evidence is mixed: one Red Hat study (grade B) puts Jev behind a prompt-injection classifier and ahead of a small content-safety classifier; the rest is grade D. TypeSafe's 67.8% is agreement with LLM reference answers, not accuracy against human labels.

Build: typesafe-sdk 0.7.2 (0.7.3 and 0.7.4 published 9 Oct, not re-audited; 0.7.4 defaults read 11 Oct: 10 s per HTTP operation, 2 retries, 30 s retry budget); @typesafe-ai/sdk 0.6.0 or AI SDK experimental_evaluate (audited at ai 7.0.122; patch releases up to ai 7.0.137 and @ai-sdk/typesafe-ai 3.0.17 by 10 Oct, not re-audited). Claude Code and MCP guardrails: only LangChain AutoModeMiddleware fails closed; @jkudish/jev-mcp keeps the audited failure path (checked at 0.14.1); oh-my-claudecode is advisory at default settings and keeps its failure path (checked at v5.6.2), defaults to a 2,000 ms timeout (250 ms up to v5.5.0) and adds OMC_JEV=<point>:active, which lets Jev decide.

n8n (3 Oct): TypeSafe's node is the scoped @typesafe-ai/n8n-nodes-typesafe-ai 0.9.0 (npm provenance to typesafe-ai tag 0.9.0; the only Jev node verified on n8n); the unscoped n8n-nodes-typesafe-ai belongs to a third party. All 5 nodes read stop the workflow on a Jev error unless Continue On Fail is on.

46 creator videos show Jev running on concrete tasks in 13 use-case groups. Products ledger (11 Oct): 99 rows, 86 grade A (Jev call read in source); 7 company and analyst production or cost claims listed, 5 rechecked on 3 Oct and 2 relayed by VentureBeat not rechecked; none is independently verified.

Reranking and RAG (8 Oct; studies updated 10 and 11 Oct): Of 4 rerunnable graded reranking-pipeline studies, 2 come from parties with a stake and 2 state none (jev-pulse, 40 queries; jev-rerank-bench, Jev level with Cohere within noise); the other grade-A study measures relevance judgments. Of 5 reranking and passage-filter implementations read at pinned commits, on a Jev error 2 stop (jev-reranker, LanceDB), 2 fall back (LlamaIndex to the retriever's order, LiteLLM to the uncompacted request) and 1 passes unscreened passages (Spring AI JevDocumentFilter). LanceDB's reranker with no key raises at the first rerank call, with no fallback (read 11 Oct).

SQL and document pipelines (8 Oct): of 5 projects read at pinned commits (pg-jev, sqlite3-jev, sqlite-jev, pg-redact, DocJev), all 5 stop the query or request on a Jev error; pg-redact stores text unredacted when a span's answer is missing or below 0.5; all 5 send row or document text out (pg-jev the whole row as JSON). The three SQL extensions return their value to the query and are not counted on When Jev fails; pg-redact and DocJev are.

Alternatives (11 Oct): Jev weights: not found on TypeSafe's site, docs, GitHub or Hugging Face (10 Oct). Of 31 listed substitutes: 12 model weights, 11 local runtimes, 4 request adapters, 2 classifier/LLM approaches, 2 hosted APIs from other providers (OpenAI, Microsoft). OpenAI's Decisions API (gpt-6-luna, public beta, text and images, $0.10 per 1M input tokens, output free) and Microsoft-Decision-1 (published 9 Oct; Microsoft says it is available in Microsoft Foundry and through OpenRouter; $0.042 per 1M input tokens, output free, as Microsoft states) are hosted APIs from other providers: your data goes to that provider. The Decisions API's graded comparisons with Jev differ by task (B38, B39); Microsoft-Decision-1 has no graded comparison. Strands Decider: copies are published by Amazon's verified Hugging Face organisation (Documented); The New Stack reports it as an AWS project (Reported). A Jev-named Ollama model was not found on Ollama's first search page (10 Oct 2026, 05:11 UTC).
uncertainty: No pool-made Jev call, account, bill, signup, mailbox connection, package install, trade, payment or eval run; the console returned HTTP 403 on 11 Oct. X could not be searched for newer TypeSafe posts.

TypeSafe's SOC 2 report is listed behind "Request access" and was not seen; what Slack and Google Workspace process for TypeSafe is not recorded; which of Vercel's two providers serves a given request, whether DigitalOcean on Vercel forwards to TypeSafe, and whether OpenRouter's ZDR listing rests on a special agreement, are not stated; Netlify's docs say its AI Gateway does not store prompts or outputs, but its other data terms were not read.
A TypeSafe retention period, human access to inputs and a Telemetry opt-out are not stated in TypeSafe's public text.
Which Kev checkpoints JevBench ran, Kev-9B's base licence, the JevAny/AnyJev identity and the operator of he-jev are unknown.
The five triage projects are code-backed but none is verified as operating; at least 70 more triage repositories were not read.
No benchmark was run or rerun by the pool; three A grades are provisional; the one graded comparison with trained classifiers (Red Hat, grade B) states no sample size and its code was not read.

Newer releases not re-audited: LiteLLM 1.104.2, typesafe-sdk 0.7.4 (defaults read only), @effect/ai-typesafe 4.0.3, @openclaw/typesafe 2026.10.1 (read up to the jev-triage branch), ai 7.0.137 and @ai-sdk/typesafe-ai 3.0.17. The exact time of the 40-to-80 requests-per-second change is unknown (the Internet Archive's 3 and 4 Oct captures are after the first observation).

What OpenRouter's Jev Router does when Jev fails and how it bills the routed model are not documented; none of the six routers or six moderation projects read in source was run, and none is verified as operating.

Email: ilyamk's granted OAuth scope and spam-leadgen's no-key behaviour are unknown; three email projects set no HTTP timeout; whether question text is billed and the tokens-per-character ratio are assumptions. n8n: core error-output handling is known only from the official node's code comment; 10 of 15 n8n packages found were not read; the declined-verification claim is Reported. Two VentureBeat-relayed production claims were not rechecked.

Trading and judges: no live order, fill or payment was observed; jev-trader's no-key path and QuantDinger's signal-to-live worker path were not traced end to end; competitor-hunter's Jev caller is not pinned; the Jevals harness code is not public. The judge rows on When Jev fails were mapped from the 4 Oct reads; openlayer jevals' no-key branch was read on 8 Oct (another configured backend, else fail-closed).

Browser agents and frameworks: no agent, package or cloud console was run, installed or logged into; failure cells are read from source and live behaviour may differ; whether computer-use-jev sends [secure] field values, second-look's fallback wording, trycua/cua's no-key behaviour and the SDK defaults inherited by LangChain and Pydantic AI were not read; AWS and Azure Marketplace results were read on the first page only.
Reddit, X, TikTok and YouTube could not be read in the daily scan; search analytics were unavailable when page topics were chosen (11 Oct run).

Coding agents and model IDs: no coding agent, plugin, hook or MCP server was installed or run; what Codex and Cursor do with a hook's answer, the Claude Code engine's handling of Hoppin-Sorter/jev-router's model rewrite, OpenCode's handling of tools removed by jev-for-all's plugin, hermes-jev-mana's key handling and the Hermes version its patch targets, OpenClaw 2026.10.1 past the line read, and whether the osuki tarballs match their tags were not read; no request was sent to any route, so what each route actually serves under an unversioned ID is not observed.

Reranking, SQL and documents (8 Oct; updated 11 Oct): no reranker, extension or pipeline was installed or run; which TypeSafe SDK version LanceDB installs (and so its timeout), PostgreSQL's result after pg-jev's uncaught ValueError and SQLite's json_extract NULL path were not read; six further SQL candidates are listed but not audited.

Alternatives and benchmarks (11 Oct): no model, runtime, plugin, proxy, Decisions API or Microsoft call was made; Microsoft-Decision-1's data terms and its OpenRouter listing were not checked (it was not in OpenRouter's model list at 11 Oct 2026, 05:17 UTC); the Enterprise page's answer on running Jev in a VPC or on-premises was not readable; TOD's base licence is not recorded; where B39's significance test is computed, B38's full call logs, classifier-bakeoff's metric code and decisionbench's results were not found or not opened; 10 new comparison repositories were seen by README only.
freshness_note: 11 October 2026 (05:16–05:40 UTC): three comparisons of Jev with a substitute graded A from files opened at pinned commits (B38–B40; 37 graded rows); the alternatives evidence cell rebuilt from graded rows and Microsoft-Decision-1 added (31 substitutes); coding-agent integrations settled (24 read; 13 act on Jev's answer); the failure checklist recounted at 74 implementations; Products 99 rows; pydantic-ai-slim 2.55.0 compared and SDK default timeouts read; access, model IDs on six routes, limits, price and the subprocessor list rechecked (unchanged); no home notice retired. Earlier reports remain dated snapshots.
